ideas.title: The basket winch: an iron-stator motor hauls a friend up the cliff
ideas.critique: This is round 1's stator idea again, but now it has a load whose weight comes from mesh volume times density and a stretchy rope, so the turns-against-heat trade-off ends in a clear lift-or-stall result and the camera has a reason to move. The danger is the friend's complaining and swinging: that is a reaction gag, and if the rope and the stall are tuned until a nice halfway stop happens, it becomes a rig about one cliff.

ideas.title: The friends' treadwheel charges the lead jar
ideas.critique: A creature whose gait slows because the current really pushes back through the wheel is something new: electricity you can see in a body's effort, and the pony-versus-crab choice is a nerdy joke. It also lands two road steps at once (dynamo and Planté jar) on top of a leg-thrust model, so the plainest version is a speed multiplier on a walk cycle feeding a charge number, with the bubbles as a look.

ideas.title: Wind your own coil: sloppy turns short themselves
ideas.critique: The player's care decides how good the motor is, through a real wire path whose touching turns the contact model finds and shorts, and that is honest and general. The scorched coil next to the neat one repeats the wire-that-overheats payoff, and a winding path laid from crank speed is likely to be a parametric helix with noise rather than wire that really piles.

ideas.title: Smelt the stator's iron from the beach's black sand
ideas.critique: Linking how the iron was smelted to coercivity, and so to the motor's drag, is a lovely chain from raw material to machine, and a glowing dusk furnace is good for the path tracer. But a bloomery 'heat and gas balance' made in one session will be a few lumped rate equations, with the carbon-to-coercivity map written in to give a soft or hard result, and the bellows rhythm is a single slider.

ideas.title: Plante's jar: form the plates by charging and reversing
ideas.critique: This is round 1's Planté idea reworded, and it is judged the same: the chemistry is real, the state is visible, it is a core road step, and coming back over days to form the plates is a good hook. The pitched film, a jar on the bench whose bubbles swap plates, is again a fixed device left alone, and the growth rate per cycle can easily be fitted to land on a nice capacity.
